details: Bitcoin experienced a downtrend, with its price dropping by 0.34% in the last 24 hours to approximately $73,591.81. This decline is part of a broader weakness, as the cryptocurrency has shed 4.12% over the past week and 3.61% over the last 30 days. The market remains volatile, with prices fluctuating between $72,512.49 and $74,514.10, and traders are closely watching key support levels.
title: Bitcoin Slides Amid Downtrend, Traders Eye Support

details: Hyperliquid's HYPE token reached a new all-time high near $70 on May 31, extending a significant monthly rally with gains exceeding 67%. The surge is attributed to strong institutional demand, with ETF products drawing $100.48 million in May inflows, and the platform's model which uses trading fees for HYPE buybacks.
title: Hyperliquid's HYPE Token Surges to New All-Time High

details: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has approved Bitcoin perpetual futures contracts for Kalshi and issued a no-action letter to Coinbase, allowing it to offer certain perpetual futures products to U.S. customers. This marks a significant step towards legalizing and integrating crypto derivatives into regulated markets, potentially shifting trading activity from offshore exchanges to compliant domestic frameworks.
title: US CFTC Approves Bitcoin Perpetual Futures for Kalshi and Coinbase

details: Paxos has become the first blockchain-native firm to receive full registration from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as a clearing agency. This landmark approval allows Paxos Securities Settlement Company to provide clearing and settlement services for U.S. stocks using blockchain technology, enabling same-day settlement and integrating blockchain infrastructure directly into traditional financial markets.
title: Paxos Receives SEC Approval as First Blockchain-Native Clearing Agency
